For x=0 with D(t,0)=D(t+1,0)=0: D(t,-1) = (1 XOR s(t,0)) AND D(t,1). The OR-difference for x>=1 decomposes as: (s(t,x) OR s(t,x+1)) XOR (s(t+p,x) OR s(t+p,x+1)) = D(t,x) XOR D(t,x+1) XOR [s(t,x) AND s(t,x+1) XOR s(t+p,x) AND s(t+p,x+1)], so the AND cross-term provides nonlinear injection absent in Rule 90 (where OR is replaced by XOR and the AND term vanishes). Sum over x>=1: M(t+1) = sum_{x>=1} D(t+1,x). Each D(t+1,x) for x>=1 depends on D(t,x-1) (linear transport rightward from left-permutivity) plus the nonlinear OR-difference. When D(t,0)=0, the x=1 term receives D(t,0)=0 from the linear part but gains the nonlinear residual. The net effect: M(t+1) >= M(t) - boundary_loss(t) + injection(t), where injection(t) >= R(t) = s(t,0) AND D(t,1) when D(t,0)=0. Periodicity of center forces D(t,0)=0 for t>=T, so injection is active whenever s(t,0)=1 and D(t,1)=1. Kopra width-two ensures D(t,1)=1 infinitely often. Lone-seed density ensures s(t,0)=1 infinitely often among those times. fatal_flaws: Fundamental arithmetic/Boolean algebra error: The candidate claims `M(t+1) >= M(t) - boundary_loss(t) + injection(t)` by treating the XOR update as real addition. For binary values, `A XOR B = A + B - 2AB`. If the right-shifted defect `D(t, x-1) = 1` and the nonlinear OR-difference term is `1`, their XOR is `0`, which *decreases* the Hamming mass `M(t)`. The nonlinear 'injection' can perfectly cancel existing mass rather than accumulating it, destroying the monotonic lower bound.

The assumption is only that the center column `c(t)` is eventually periodic. This does not automatically force the entire spatial configuration or the right half-line to be periodic, even within a finite lightcone. If it did, the main open problem would be trivially solved.

rejected_candidates.title: Defect support drift: lone-seed left-expanding defect envelope forces unbounded rightward leakage incompatible with periodic center
rejected_candidates.structural_text: D(t,x) = s(t+p,x) ⊕ s(t,x) for the lone-seed Rule 30 orbit. L(t) = min{x : D(t,x)≠0}, R(t) = max{x : D(t,x)≠0}, W(t) = R(t) - L(t). If D(t,x')=0 for all x'≤x, then D(t+1,x') = s(t+p,x'-1)⊕s(t,x'-1) ⊕ [(s(t+p,x') OR s(t+p,x'+1)) ⊕ (s(t,x') OR s(t,x'+1))]. For x'≤x+1, the first term is 0 (since x'-1≤x), and s(t+p,x')=s(t,x'), s(t+p,x'+1)=s(t,x'+1) when x'<x+1 and x'+1≤x+1, giving D(t+1,x')=0 for x'≤x. Hence L(t+1)≥L(t)+1 when L(t) is the leftmost defect. Combine (a) L(t+1)≥L(t)+1 so L(t)≥L(0)+t→+∞, with (b) Kopra Corollary 3.7: for Rule 30 lone-seed, the width-two trace (s(t,0),s(t,1)) is not eventually periodic under any time shift p, hence D(t,x)≠0 for some x∈{0,1} infinitely often. However, at the boundary $x'=x$, the updated defect $D(t+1,x)$ depends on the right neighbor $s(t,x+1)$ due to the $(b \lor c)$ term in the rule. If $s(t,x)=0$, this reduces to $D(t+1,x) = D(t,x+1) = 1$. Thus, the defect expands leftward to $x$, meaning $L(t+1) \le L(t)-1$. rejected_candidates.title: Defect annihilation obstruction via lone-seed right-boundary parity and left-permutive rightward propagation
